primary_goal: Identify the exact background music playing during the broadcast represented by the supplied CRT-TV photograph.

source_asset.forensic_constraint: A still image contains no audio fingerprint, so exact track identification requires either a matched archival recording of the same broadcast or an audio/video sample from the source footage.

game_family.label: Fehlerbild / spot-the-difference image comparison
game_family.basis: The two near-identical images and contemporary descriptions of 9Live Fehlerbild formats strongly match the observed composition.

person_identification.note: No person in the supplied image is identified from appearance.

broadcast_attribution.best_current_attribution: 9Live or a 9Live-produced Call-TV window on another ProSiebenSat.1-family channel
broadcast_attribution.important_caveat: The absence of a clearly readable channel bug means a 9Live-produced block on another broadcaster remains possible.
supporting_evidence: The observed lower-third is consistent with the German 01379 mass-calling era and 9Live's visual/call-in mechanics.
Historical sources document 9Live's well-known 01379/444999 participation number and roughly EUR 0.49 per fixed-network call.
Contemporary sources explicitly describe 9Live Fehlerbild games based on two nearly identical images.
9Live also produced call-in quiz windows for other ProSiebenSat.1 channels, so production identity and channel identity must not be conflated.

basis: Fehlerbild games are documented on 9Live by 2003.
01379/444999 is explicitly documented in 2004 and remained in use later.
The visual style and CRT-era capture are compatible with the mid-2000s.
date_estimate.not_yet_resolved: Exact broadcast date, time and program title.

phone_and_tariff.tariff: approximately EUR 0.49 per call from the German fixed network in the relevant period
phone_and_tariff.note: CRT moire makes individual digits in the supplied frame less reliable than independent historical confirmation of the canonical 9Live number.

key_discovery.evidence: A surviving German trance-forum thread titled '9live Track gesucht' included a sample described as 9Live background music; on 16 December 2004 the requester reported the identification as Brainbug - Nightmare (Burger Queens Remix).
key_discovery.why_it_is_currently_the_lead: It is the strongest directly documented 9Live background-track identification found inside the likely visual era of the photograph. It is not yet tied to this exact Fehlerbild broadcast.

other_documented_tracks_or_music_reports.evidence: Contemporary fan report says 9Live was using 'Reality' as background music; a later post in the same thread says 9Live played multiple tracks from the first Altromondo CD.
Later viewer discussions list it among music heard on 9Live.
other_documented_tracks_or_music_reports.relevance_to_exact_frame: LOWER; documentation found is later than the strongest estimated frame period

other_documented_tracks_or_music_reports.evidence: Later viewer discussions list it among music heard on 9Live.

production_music_behavior: Contemporary descriptions state that dramatic music and ticking were used to create urgency before a caller was connected.
A 2004 discussion notes that presenters could announce a 'last' music change as a signal that a game was supposedly nearing its end.

In 2006 the 9Live viewer editorial office reportedly wrote that it did not list the music titles and that there was no general playlist, strongly indicating rotating music rather than one universal theme.

required_for_high_confidence: find an archival video containing this exact woman-and-dog Fehlerbild and compare its soundtrack
or obtain approximately 5-15 seconds of audio/video from the source recording and perform direct music matching/comparison

historical_context.call_selection: Contemporary reporting describes 9Live's Hot Button mechanism and long intervals before an incoming caller was connected.
historical_context.prize_example: A documented 9Live viewing session describes a caller eventually winning EUR 1,000 after dramatic music and ticking, matching the same general prize/pressure pattern visible in the supplied frame.
historical_context.fehlerbild_context: Contemporary discussions document both single-error and many-error image-comparison variants, including criticism that some differences were extremely difficult to see on ordinary television sets.
